# isConsistent2DArray

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a non-empty matrix whose rows all have the same length.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isConsistent2DArray() — Checks whether a value is a non-empty matrix whose rows all have the same length. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/array</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isConsistent2DArray(arr: unknown): arr is Array<Array<unknown>>;
```

This is the check to run before `Range#setValues`, which rejects a ragged matrix with a message that names neither
the offending row nor the reason. Everything [`is2DArray`](is2DArray.md) requires holds here as well — a non-empty
array of arrays — plus the rule that every row is as wide as the first.

As a TypeScript type predicate it narrows the value to `Array<Array<unknown>>` inside the branch.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `arr`     | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` if the value is a non-empty array of arrays of equal length; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `arr` to `Array<Array<unknown>>` inside the branch.

## Examples

### Uniform rows, ragged rows, and non-matrices

```javascript
isConsistent2DArray([
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4]
]); // => true
isConsistent2DArray([[1, 2], [3]]); // => false — rows differ in length
isConsistent2DArray([1, 2]); // => false — not 2D at all
isConsistent2DArray([]); // => false
```

### Before writing to a range

<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="isConsistent2DArray.ts" include-symbol="write"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function write(sheet, rows) {
  if (!isConsistent2DArray(rows)) {
    throw new Error("Every row must have the same number of columns.");
  }
  sheet.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, rows[0].length).setValues(rows);
}
</code-block>
</tab>
</tabs>
